title: audit JsonlFileLogger doc claims O_APPEND atomic writes but events can exceed PIPE_BUF
description: audit.rs JsonlFileLogger documentation states writes are atomic by O_APPEND. O_APPEND atomic guarantee only holds for writes <= PIPE_BUF (4096 bytes on Linux). A single audit event serialized as JSON (e.g. with long header fields or a large body preview) can easily exceed 4096 bytes, at which point two concurrent writers will interleave bytes and produce malformed JSONL. Either: (a) serialize events to a channel and let a single writer task append, or (b) acquire a file lock per write, or (c) document the limit and enforce a max event size.
